- File: scripts/unblock_judge.sh
- Location: unblock_run_ops remove_label case, the `grep -q 'HTTP 404'` branch (LAST RUN DIFF hunk at lines ~168-175)
  PROBLEM: The 404-detection is a literal substring match on the `gh` stderr text "HTTP 404" (e.g. `gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)`). The check is case-sensitive and assumes `gh` keeps that exact format. If a future `gh` release changes the wording (different casing, omits the "HTTP " prefix, splits the words, or localizes the message), real failures (HTTP 500, network errors, auth failures) would still match a substring of "404" if any happens to appear, while real 404s would stop matching and the next op (and the resume command) would be silently blocked — re-introducing the bug the diff is fixing.
  WHY: The test fixture writes the exact format the grep expects, so this fragility is invisible to CI. The reviewer describes this as advisory hardening rather than a runtime failure in the current code.
  HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3
